task.title: Compare Changes Before Committing
task.shortdesc: See exactly what changed in a file (including images) before you stage or commit.

step.cmd: In the or area, double-click the file.

result.p: The compare editor opens and highlights the differences between your version and the last committed version. Because a newly added file has no version in the last commit, double-clicking it opens the file instead. The exception is a file that you staged and then edited again, because the staged row has its own content to display.

Each pane is labeled with the version it displays. For an unstaged file, the comparison is between Working copy and Last commit, or between Working copy and Staged if the same file also has staged changes. For a staged file, the comparison is between Staged and Last commit.
When the file is one that this working copy adds, the second pane is empty and is labeled Last commit - file did not exist yet.

A staged row always shows what it contributes to the next commit. Therefore, for a file that you edited again after staging it, use the Open action to open the staged version in read-only mode. Use to open the editable file from the working copy. A staged row on the row in the Git History view shows and opens the same versions as in the view.
result.note: For image files (PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, TIFF, and other raster formats), the Git Client opens a side-by-side image comparison, with the newer version on the left and the older version on the right. SVG files are treated as XML, so they open in the regular text comparison (where you can switch to Author mode to see them rendered).
